request.name: Search for one car, live from the Ninja API, with a database fallback

description.content:
Unlike `GET /cars`, this calls api-ninjas.com live. The free Ninja
tier only ever returns one car per request, so this always returns
at most one — there is no way to page or bulk-search live.

If the live call succeeds, the result is upserted into the local
`cars` table and returned with `source: ninja_api`. If it fails
for any reason (bad key, network error, Ninja down) — or succeeds
but has no match for this brand/year — the local `cars` table is
queried instead, and the response comes back with
`source: database_fallback`. Only if neither has a match does
this return `404`.

REST API for the car rental booking app.

Almost every endpoint is plain synchronous request/response. The one
exception is **POST /bookings** — it writes the booking as `pending`,
publishes an event to RabbitMQ, and returns `202 Accepted` immediately.
A human admin approves or rejects it later via the admin endpoints;
the customer finds out by polling `GET /bookings/{id}`.

Authentication is JWT (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`) for every route
except register/login. There is no separate admin table — the login
endpoint checks the submitted email against `ADMIN_EMAIL` in `.env`
first, and issues a token with `role: admin` if it matches.
